record.original_question: Fix n and d, and let D_{n,d} be the generic number of eigenscheme points for degree-d forms in n+1 variables. Let E_{n,d} denote the Zariski-closed locus in the symmetrized product (PV)^(·D_{n,d}) (equivalently in Hilb_{D_{n,d}}(PV)) consisting of eigenconfigurations that occur as eigenschemes X_f of some f ∈ S^dV. Determine defining equations (in the broad Zariski-closed-condition sense) for E_{n,d}.

evidence.quote: For every d, one deﬁnes a variety of eigenconfigurations En,d = {(v1 , . . . , vDn,d ) ∈ (PV )(·Dn,d ) : Xf = {v1 , . . . , vDn,d } for some f ∈ S d V }.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ with coordinates $x_0,\dots,x_n$, and let $S^dV$ denote the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in these variables. For $f \in S^dV$, the eigenscheme $X_f \subset \mathbb{P}V$ is the closed subscheme defined by the $2\times 2$ minors of the matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix} x_0 & x_1 & \cdots & x_n \\ \partial f/\partial x_0 & \partial f/\partial x_1 & \cdots & \partial f/\partial x_n \end{pmatrix},$$
i.e., the locus of points $v \in \mathbb{P}V$ such that $\nabla f(v)$ is proportional to $v$. For generic $f$, $X_f$ consists of a fixed number $D_{n,d}$ of reduced points (the generic eigenscheme cardinality, equal to $\sum_{i=0}^{n}(d-1)^i$).

Define the eigenconfiguration variety
$$E_{n,d} = \overline{\{(v_1,\dots,v_{D_{n,d}}) \in (\mathbb{P}V)^{(\cdot D_{n,d})} : X_f = \{v_1,\dots,v_{D_{n,d}}\} \text{ for some } f \in S^dV\}}$$
inside the symmetric product $(\mathbb{P}V)^{(\cdot D_{n,d})}$ (equivalently inside $\mathrm{Hilb}_{D_{n,d}}(\mathbb{P}V)$); this is a Zariski-closed subset.

Problem: Determine explicit defining equations (polynomial conditions cutting out the Zariski-closed locus) for $E_{n,d}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining defining equations for the eigenconfiguration variety $E_{n,d}$ is posed as an open problem in the literature on tensor eigenschemes and symmetric tensor decomposition. No general answer has been found; partial results are known only for special small cases (e.g., $n=1$, related to binary forms, where eigenconfigurations are well understood). No search evidence indicates a general solution.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvectors of tensors and related literature (arXiv 2304.10570 context)
status_evidence.snippet: The variety of eigenconfigurations E_{n,d} is introduced and the problem 'Determine equations for E_{n,d}' is explicitly posed.
status_evidence.claim: The question of defining equations for E_{n,d} is stated as an open problem.
